title: React Query for Server State
description: Master TanStack Query (React Query) for managing server state, including caching, background refetching, mutations, and devtools integration.

data.text: Server state is different from local state in ways that matter. It lives somewhere else. It can change without your app knowing about it. It needs to be cached, deduplicated, and kept in sync with the outside world. **TanStack Query** (formerly React Query) was built specifically for these problems.

Instead of storing API responses in `useState` and writing complex `useEffect` hooks to fetch and refetch data, React Query gives you a cache with sensible defaults: data is cached by query key, stale data is refetched in the background, and duplicate requests are automatically deduplicated.

items: Query keys uniquely identify each piece of server data in the cache
Queries are functions that return a promise — React Query caches the result
Stale time determines how long data is considered fresh before refetching
Mutations handle creating, updating, and deleting data, then invalidate related queries

data.text: The `useQuery` hook takes a unique query key and a function that fetches data. React Query handles the loading, error, and success states for you. It also caches the result so subsequent components using the same key do not trigger duplicate network requests.

data.title: Fetching Posts with useQuery

data.text: Mutations are actions that change data on the server: creating a new post, updating a comment, deleting an item. After a mutation succeeds, you typically want to update the cache so the UI reflects the change immediately. React Query makes this easy with `invalidateQueries`.

data.title: Creating a Post with useMutation

data.text: Query keys are arrays that form a hierarchy. `['posts']` matches all posts. `['posts', postId]` matches a single post. `['posts', { filter: 'draft' }]` matches filtered posts. This hierarchy means you can invalidate broadly or precisely. Invalidating `['posts']` refetches all post-related queries; invalidating `['posts', '123']` refetches only that one post.

data.title: DevTools
data.text: Install the React Query DevTools browser extension or add them in development mode. They show you every query in the cache, its status, when it last fetched, and what it is waiting on. This visibility alone will change how you debug data-fetching issues.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: React Query manages server state with caching, deduplication, and background refetching
useQuery handles fetching; useMutation handles creating, updating, and deleting
Query keys form a hierarchy that controls cache invalidation
Prefer React Query over useState for any data that comes from an API
